items.title: Banks NPL declined to 13.1% in October 2026
items.description: The Non-Performing Loan (NPL) ratio in the banking industry declined to 13.1% in October 2026 from 19.5% over the same period the previous year. According to the Bank of Ghana, this was supported by the strong rebound in credit and a contraction in the stock of NPLs. At the same time, the Capital Adequacy Ratio rose to 18.5% in October 2026, from 17.9% a year earlier. Asset quality also improved markedly, showing that the financial soundness indicators improved broadly. In the first eight months of 2026, Banks operating in Ghana wrote off GH¢1.86 billion as bad debt as of August 2026. This is a 76.3% increase over GH¢1.05 billion recorded during the same period in 2025. According to the Banks’ Income Statement published by the Bank of Ghana, the provision is made up of loan losses, depreciation, among others. The banks’ operating expenses also rose by 6.4% to GH¢13.25 billion in August 2026. Meanwhile, asset quality indicators improved during the review period, with the Non-Performing Loan ratio declining to 15.7% in August 2026 from 20.8% a year earlier, while the adjusted NPL ratio fell to 3.8% from 6.8%.

items.title: World: Ending violence against children: From commitment to reality
items.description: Country: World Source: UN Children's Fund Please refer to the attached file. Violence against children remains one of the most widespread violations of children’s rights worldwide. Despite global commitments to end all forms of violence against children, millions of children continue to experience violence across regions and income levels, revealing the persistent gap between commitment and reality. This brief presents the latest available global estimates on violent discipline by caregivers in the home and sexual violence in childhood, drawing on evidence from both development and humanitarian contexts. The brief illustrates why accelerating progress towards SDG Target 16.2 remains an urgent priority and highlights the essential role of both universal and targeted prevention efforts and a strong, accessible social service workforce equipped with a package of evidence-based family support and child protection services. Accelerating progress will require renewed political commitment, sustained investment, stronger child protection systems capable of delivering evidence-based services at scale in cooperation with allied services such as health, education, and justice, and the large-scale implementation of proven universal and targeted prevention interventions.

items.title: Konga shows tech-enabled retail platforms can complement conventional healthcare delivery
items.description: By Prince Osuagwu The growing intersection of technology, healthcare and e-commerce is opening new opportunities for mobile health delivery in Nigeria. This is as one of Nigeria’s composite e-commerce companies Konga attracted the partnership of global skincare brand, La Roche-Posay, to expand access to dermatological expertise and authentic skincare products in the country. The partnership, leverages Konga Health’s retail and e-commerce network to connect consumers with genuine dermatological products, professional skincare advice and health education. The partnership sealed in Lagos recently, demonstrated how technology-enabled retail platforms could complement conventional healthcare delivery by making specialist skincare products and information more accessible to consumers. La Roche-Posay, a brand under L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty, partnered with Konga Health, its official distributor in Nigeria, to promote dermatological science, product authenticity and informed skincare choices. A major attraction was the interactive skin science experience, which allowed visitors to explore common skin conditions, including hyperpigmentation, acne, damaged skin barriers, dryness and the effects of ultraviolet radiation. The programme also featured free consultations with certified dermatologists and members of the L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty MedSquad, who provided professional skin analysis, guidance and practical recommendations. Among the participating specialists were Dr Ayesha Akinkugbe, dermatologist and Vice-President of the Nigerian Association of Dermatologists, and Dr Folakemi Cole-Adeife. The event showcased five major La Roche-Posay product franchises: Cicaplast for skin repair, Mela B3 for hyperpigmentation, Anthelios for sun protection, Lipikar for dry and atopic-prone skin, and Effaclar for acne-prone skin. Speaking at the event, Leo Stan Ekeh, Chairman of Zinox Group, said the commercial opportunities in Nigeria’s beauty and personal-care market, was enormous. He added that the importance of bringing globally recognised brands and quality products closer to Nigerian consumers can never be overemphasised. For Anaïs Routhiau, Business Development Manager, LID LDB SSA, the Living Lab provided an opportunity to bring La Roche-Posay’s commitment to dermatological science closer to consumers, helping them better understand their skin and the science behind the products they use. Beyond the medical engagements, the partnership addresses a growing challenge in Nigeria’s skincare market: access to genuine products and reliable health information. Through Konga Health’s distribution and e-commerce infrastructure, consumers can access authentic L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty products through an authorised channel, reducing exposure to counterfeit products and unreliable sellers. The initiative underscores the growing role of digital commerce in mobile health, particularly in connecting consumers to specialised healthcare products and professional guidance beyond conventional hospital settings. Other personalities at the event included Prince Nnamdi Ekeh, CEO of Konga Group; Mrs Chioma Ekeh, Group CEO of TD Africa; Yvonne Enwerem, Vice-President of Konga Health; and representatives of L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty. Also present were actor Osas Ighodaro, who served as Chief Living Lab Officer; health educator Dr Chinonso Egemba, popularly known as Aproko Doctor; media personality Mimi Onalaja; and beauty entrepreneur Subuola Oyeleye. The collaboration highlights how the convergence of digital retail, medical expertise and consumer education can strengthen access to dermatological healthcare while building trust in Nigeria’s expanding beauty and personal-care market. The post Konga shows tech-enabled retail platforms can complement conventional healthcare delivery appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: World: A record high of nearly one in four children now live in conflict zones - Save the Children report
items.description: Country: World Source: Save the Children · Nearly one in four children worldwide live in conflict zones, new report finds · Africa now accounts for 44% of children living near conflict worldwide, with an unprecedented two in five African children impacted · Verified incidents of denial of humanitarian access against children have increased almost 16-fold in a decade to almost one an hour AMMAN, 19 November 2026 – Almost one in four children worldwide are now living in conflict zones, the highest number since records began in 1990, according to a new Save the Children report. The figure represents an increase of more than 50% in a decade, jumping from 378 million in 2015 to 589 million in 2025, according to the report Stop the War on Children: Changing the Odds , which draws on data from the Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO). The report found that the share of the world’s children living in conflict zones more than doubled from about 10% in the mid-1990s to 23.4% in 2025. Africa is home to the highest number of children living in conflict zones, accounting for about 260 million, or 44% of the global total. This is nearly a 20% increase from the 218 million children in Africa who lived in conflict zones in 2024. Across Africa, the proportion of children living in conflict zones more than tripled from about one in eight children in 2010 to about two in five in 2025, the highest level ever recorded for the continent. This puts Africa on par with the Middle East, where both regions now have two in five children living in conflict zones. Elsewhere, about one in four children (24.2%) in the Americas lived in conflict zones in 2025, one in seven (14.3%) in Asia, and nearly one in nine (10.6%) in Europe. The report also examined United Nations verified grave violations against children in armed conflict between 2005 and 2025, including killing and maiming, recruitment by armed forces or groups, sexual violence, abduction, attacks on schools and hospitals, and denial of humanitarian access. These numbers represent the tip of the iceberg for grave violations against children, as most attacks on children go unverified, said Save the Children. Killing and maiming accounted for the largest share of violations against children over the past two decades, with 171,712 cases verified since 2005. More than 70% of the cases were committed against children in five countries: the occupied Palestinian territory, Afghanistan, Somalia, Syria and Yemen. The report also found that the fastest-growing grave violation against children is the denial of humanitarian aid, with verified incidents skyrocketing from 509 in 2015 to 8,322 in 2025, more than a 16-fold increase in a decade. This amounts to almost one verified incident of denial of humanitarian aid every hour, on average, in 2025. More than 70% of all verified aid denial last year took place against Palestinian children. Denial of humanitarian access rose from just over 2% of all verified grave violations in 2015 to more than 21% in 2025, making it the second most frequently verified violation after killing and maiming. Rape and other forms of sexual violence against children are widely underreported. Even so, the report found that 28,909 cases have been verified since reporting began. The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) accounts for 12,698, or almost 44% of the total, followed by Somalia with 4,534 and Chad with 2,979. Together, the three countries account for around 70% of all verified cases. In eastern DRC, 17-year-old Ana* experienced the devastating consequences of conflict after violence forced her family from their home. After months of displacement, they returned, only for armed men to break into their house, shoot Ana’s brother dead and rape her while other family members were assaulted. “We had fled the war, but it came knocking at our door again. [When the attackers came to our home] I screamed; I begged for mercy… but no one listened. My brother was killed before my eyes. I was raped,” Ana said. “[Afterwards] the hardest part wasn’t the pain. It was people’s mockery. They pointed fingers at me, as if I were to blame for what had been done to me.” The next morning, neighbours helped Ana reach a local health centre supported by Save the Children, where she received emergency medical care, including treatment to prevent pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections, as well as ongoing psychosocial support. Gudrun Østby, Research Professor at PRIO, said: “We estimate that 589 million children were living close to armed conflict last year. These record-high figures are a stark reminder that conflict is devastating the daily lives, education, health and future prospects of hundreds of millions of children. Unless greater efforts are made to protect children in conflict settings, the consequences of today's wars will be felt for decades to come.” Inger Ashing, CEO of Save the Children International, said: “Almost one in four children around the world now lives in a conflict zone. What could be more important than their protection? The scale of this crisis is rapidly growing, and the systems meant to protect children are being pushed to breaking point. “We're seeing aid weaponised, attacked and deliberately disrupted. Humanitarian organisations are denied access, funding is being slashed, and needs are outpacing our ability to reach every child in crisis. Meanwhile, parties to conflict continue to disregard the rules of war, while new military technologies are changing how wars are fought, increasing the risk further for children in conflict settings. “Children’s rights and needs must be at the centre of decisions about war, peace and security. More than 20 years of monitoring violations have made the horrors children face visible and created opportunities to prevent further harm. This work must be protected, supported and translated into action. "Parties to conflict must uphold the rules of war, and those responsible for violations must be held to account. But ensuring the protection of children isn’t only the responsibility of those fighting. States, donors and companies with leverage over perpetrators must use it, through diplomatic and political pressure. To truly change the odds for children living in conflict zones, we must put their protection first and work towards the peace they deserve.” Save the Children is calling on parties to the conflict to uphold international humanitarian law, accounting for children’ distinct vulnerabilities, and to facilitate safe and unimpeded humanitarian relief to civilians. It is also urging governments to strengthen accountability for violations against children, implement international treaties and declarations that protect children and education in war zones, address the root causes of conflict and ensure children’s voices are heard in decisions affecting their futures. In 2025, Save the Children worked in 107 countries, reaching more than 58.2 million people, including 37.8 million children. The child rights organisation also responded to 113 humanitarian crises in 63 countries, supporting over 24 million people, including 13.6 million children. ENDS Notes to Editor: Read the full report here: https://resourcecentre.savethechildren.net/document/stop-the-war-on-children-changing-the-odds-2026 · The updated analysis on the number and share of children living in conflict zones is conducted by the Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO). The core dataset used to map conflict patterns in this report is the Uppsala Conflict Data Program’s Georeferenced Event Data Set (UCDP GED) until 2025. To estimate the number of children living in conflict areas, and populations more generally, PRIO integrated the UCDP conflict data with population data from CIESIN’s Gridded Population of the World (GPW) and from the UN World Population Prospects. PRIO uses UCDP’s definition of armed conflict: ‘armed force used by an organized actor against another organized actor, or against civilians, resulting in at least 25 battle-related deaths in one calendar year’. A ‘conflict zone’ is defined as an area within 50km of where one or more conflict incidents take place in a given year, within the borders of a country. · The UN Security Council has identified six grave violations against children in situations of armed conflict: killing and maiming of children; recruitment or use of children by armed forces and groups; sexual violence against children; abduction of children; attacks against schools and hospitals; and denial of humanitarian access for children. These grave violations were defined on the basis of their egregious nature and their severe impact on children’s wellbeing. · Stop the War on Children

items.title: Claude-maker Anthropic poised for more than $1.4tn stock market debut
items.description: Anthropic is poised to hit a value of more than $1.4 trillion (£1.1 trillion) when it debuts on the public stock market. The artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the popular chatbot Claude said it will price shares at $83 each when it lists on Thursday on the Nasdaq, a tech-focused stock exchange based in New York. That price will make it one of the most highly valued companies in the world. It will be the first US firm focused exclusively on AI to go public, marking a crucial test for the fast-growing industry, which faces questions over whether the huge investment poured into the technology will be profitable. The AI firm said earlier this month it would likely offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each, which valued the company at up to $1.3tn. But demand for Anthropic’s stock debut – commonly referred to as its initial public offering, or IPO – is very high, according to one early investor in the company who spoke with the BBC on condition of anonymity. The person said shares were more than 10 times oversubscribed ahead of the public listing, meaning demand for Anthropic shares exceeded the number of shares available. If that turns out to be the case, Anthropic’s valuation could quickly blow past its target on Thursday when trading begins. Crucial test for AI Depending on how strong that demand is, Anthropic could even exceed the early market valuation of Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which was the world’s most highly valued stock debut when it went public with a value of $2.2tn in June. However, in the weeks that followed, SpaceX shares fell significantly in price . As it stands, Anthropic’s listing will see the firm raise more than $68bn from its initial investors. It is also expecting another $26bn from private placements. So the total amount the company will raise is expected to be $94bn. The amount of cash Anthropic has raised from its listing is already more than SpaceX raised in June . OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and Anthropic’s biggest AI rival, is expected to go public next year. Until then, Anthropic will be the only public company in the US that is entirely focused on the technology, or one that was founded and built around AI tools and products. Its scope is different from tech giants like Google and Microsoft that also develop AI but are involved in other tech services. There is excitement around Anthropic’s listing, but also some concern from investors around its ability to generate revenue and profits going forward. Yang Wang, a principle financial analyst with Counterpoint Research, said the central issue for Anthropic is whether its business “can keep pace” as hundreds of billions of dollars in financial obligations come due in the next couple of years. “Nevertheless, it is not an everyday occurrence for public investors to gain direct exposure to a frontier-model developer with the potential to shape the next stage of productivity,” Wang said. While nearly every other major tech company is pouring huge amounts of money into the technology and infrastructure required for their own AI tools, they are built around social media or online retail or online search. AI tools and applications are secondary. “Anthropic going public gives us a whole new window into what AI demand looks like,” Marta Norton, who heads investment strategy at investment firm Empower, told the BBC. Anthropic was started by a group of co-founders , led by siblings Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, all of whom left their work at OpenAI to start a new AI firm. The company has carved itself out in the ongoing AI race as more focused on building the technology with safety top of mind. It refused to comply with a demand by the US Department of Defense that Anthropic’s tools be used in an essentially unrestricted way. And Dario Amodei has been outspoken in his belief that AI tools may soon be so powerful that they present a threat to human existence. Nonetheless, the company is looking to grow quickly and gain more access to financing through the public markets in order to do so. Norton said Anthropic going public now, in a time of market volatility comes down to the simple fact that the company needs access to more money. “AI is financially demanding,” Norton said. “The public markets open up the financial spigot a little bit more, and so the time has come.” But broader anxieties have started to grow about the AI industry’s business model, which is reliant on expensive computer chips that are in short supply. The technology is also dependent on controversial data centres and funding such operations require deals with other tech companies. The Federal Reserve Bank has expressed concern about the rapid growth of AI-related debt being financed through “complex and opaque” structures, according to minutes from its October meeting to discuss a potential rate rise. A few of the meeting’s participants also noted that “AI-related exposures were becoming increasingly concentrated among a small number of firms”.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Fin de l’opération de rapatriement des orpailleurs burkinabè en Guinée avec 70 126 personnes déjà rapatriées
items.description: Fin des opérations de rapatriement des Burkinabè affectés par les événements en Guinée selon la télévision nationale burkinabè. Au 17 novembre 2026, un total de 70 126 personnes avaient été accueillies et prises en charge, selon un communiqué du Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR). Le Burkina Faso poursuit les opérations de rapatriement de ses ressortissants affectés par les événements survenus en Guinée. Dans un communiqué publié le 17 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, le Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR) annonce avoir accueilli, enregistré et pris en charge 1 745 personnes supplémentaires au cours de cette journée. Ce nouveau mouvement porte à 70 126 le nombre total de personnes rapatriées depuis le début des opérations. Selon les chiffres communiqués par le CONASUR, cet effectif comprend 68 779 hommes et 1 347 femmes. Parmi les personnes accueillies figurent également 14 743 enfants et 1 962 ressortissants d'autres nationalités. Ces derniers ont été recensés dans le cadre des opérations de retour. Plus de 13 000 personnes convoyées vers leurs localités d'origine Au-delà de l'accueil et de l'enregistrement des rapatriés, les autorités burkinabè s’emploient à faciliter leur retour dans leurs localités d'origine. Grâce à la mobilisation des populations et des acteurs régionaux, les Conseils régionaux de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR) ont assuré le convoyage de 13 225 personnes depuis Bobo-Dioulasso vers leurs localités d'origine. Ces déplacements viennent s'ajouter aux initiatives individuelles de retour. Le CONASUR a salué la contribution des différents acteurs impliqués dans cette opération, notamment les populations mobilisées dans les régions administratives, dont la solidarité participe à l'accompagnement des personnes rapatriées. Le CONASUR appelle à privilégier les sources officielles Tout en réaffirmant sa détermination à poursuivre les opérations de rapatriement, le Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation a exprimé sa reconnaissance à l'ensemble des partenaires et des citoyens pour leur engagement. L'institution a également invité les populations à maintenir leur élan de solidarité et à faire preuve de responsabilité dans le partage des informations relatives à ces opérations. Elle recommande notamment de privilégier les sources et les canaux officiels afin d'éviter la propagation d'informations non vérifiées. Avec 70 126 personnes déjà rapatriées, l'opération représente un important défi d'accueil, d'assistance et de réinstallation pour les structures mobilisées. Au-delà des chiffres, il s'agit surtout d'accompagner des milliers de personnes contraintes de quitter leur cadre de vie et de faciliter leur retour auprès de leurs communautés d'origine. Burkina Faso : Après avoir fourni Internet aux terroristes pendant un an, Yacouba regrette sa collaboration
items.description: Ancien promoteur de WiFi dans le village d’Ira, dans le Sourou, Yacouba, 38 ans, reconnaît avoir facilité les communications de groupes terroristes entre 2024 et 2025. Devenu lui-même déplacé après le déguerpissement de son village par ces mêmes groupes, il demande pardon et appelle les autres complices à rompre avec les criminels. Un an durant, il a mis sa connexion Internet au service de groupes terroristes. Aujourd’hui, Yacouba, 38 ans, affirme regretter profondément cette collaboration. Dans un témoignage rapporté par l’Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB), cet ancien promoteur de WiFi invite ceux qui continuent d’apporter leur soutien aux groupes armés à mettre fin à leurs activités et à se ressaisir. Originaire du village d’Ira, dans la commune de Din, dans le Sourou, Yacouba explique avoir accueilli à son domicile des individus appartenant à des groupes terroristes qui venaient utiliser sa connexion Internet pour communiquer. Selon son récit, ces visites avaient particulièrement lieu les jours de marché. « Ils venaient souvent en binôme, souvent en grand nombre. Ils étaient chaque fois armés et munis de postes émetteurs-récepteurs », raconte-t-il. Il ajoute que certains préparaient même du thé à son domicile lors de leurs passages. Cette collaboration, qui s’est étendue de 2024 à 2025, a finalement pris fin dans des circonstances qu’il dit n’avoir pas anticipées. Les mêmes groupes auxquels il fournissait un accès à Internet ont contraint les habitants d’Ira à quitter leur village. Yacouba a lui aussi été obligé de partir. Il vit désormais en situation de déplacement. Une expérience qu’il présente comme une douloureuse leçon sur la nature de ses anciens partenaires. « Ces gens n’ont pas d’amis. Malgré le service que je leur rendais, ils n’ont pas hésité à déguerpir mon propre village, faisant de moi un nécessiteux », déplore-t-il. « Je demande pardon aux autorités et à l’ensemble des Burkinabè » Conscient de la gravité de son implication, Yacouba reconnaît avoir commis une erreur en facilitant les communications de ces groupes. Il exprime ses regrets et sollicite le pardon des autorités ainsi que celui de la population burkinabè. « En toute franchise, ce fut une grosse erreur pour moi de collaborer avec les terroristes et je regrette sincèrement mon acte. Je demande vraiment pardon aux autorités et à l’ensemble des Burkinabè », affirme-t-il. Son témoignage intervient dans un contexte où plusieurs autres personnes interpellées pour leur implication présumée dans les activités de groupes terroristes ont également livré leurs récits et appelé leurs anciens collaborateurs à abandonner ces pratiques. En mai 2026, Bila, un commerçant de 28 ans installé à Soudougui, dans le Koulpélogo, avait reconnu avoir participé à la logistique de groupes terroristes. Il aurait notamment fourni des vivres, du carburant et des engins, tout en écoulant des biens issus de pillages. Interpellé à Comin-Yanga, il avait appelé les autres complices à se rendre. En août 2026, dans la zone de Thiou, dans le Yatenga, Boukaré, un berger de 36 ans, avait également été interpellé. Selon les informations rapportées, il utilisait un poste émetteur-récepteur pour alerter les groupes armés de l’arrivée d’aéronefs militaires. Après avoir été pris en charge par les Forces combattantes, il avait demandé pardon au peuple burkinabè. En avril 2026, deux jeunes recrues, Bourahima et Hamadou, avaient pour leur part réussi à quitter leur base avant d’être interceptées et soignées par les Forces combattantes. Un appel à rompre avec les groupes armés À travers son témoignage, Yacouba souhaite que son parcours serve d'avertissement à ceux qui continuent de soutenir les groupes terroristes, que ce soit par la fourniture de moyens de communication, de renseignements ou d'appuis logistiques. Il les exhorte à rompre avec ces groupes et à privilégier la dénonciation de leurs activités auprès des autorités compétentes. « Nous devons obéir à nos seules autorités et arrêter de pactiser avec ces criminels. Il faut tout simplement les combattre ou les dénoncer », lance-t-il. Au-delà des regrets exprimés, le récit de Yacouba met en lumière les conséquences humaines de la crise sécuritaire. Celui qui facilitait autrefois les communications de groupes armés se retrouve aujourd'hui parmi les populations contraintes de quitter leur localité. Un changement de situation qu'il présente désormais comme une leçon et qui motive son appel à ceux qui continuent de collaborer avec ces groupes. LBMA certification key to adding Ghanaian gold to bank reserves – Ken Ashigbey
items.description: Ghana’s effort to refine all artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold locally must be matched by responsible sourcing and traceability if the country is to secure better returns, Dr Ken Ashigbey said. The government’s 2027 Budget targets 100% local refining of ASM gold by 2028. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Wednesday, the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Chamber of Mines said Ghana was already refining almost all the ASM gold it receives. “We have two refineries: the Gold Coast Refinery and the Royal Ghana Gold Refinery, which are refining ASM gold,” he said, adding that the Gold Board had driven the process. He said some gold was still being smuggled. But local refining alone does not meet the requirements for gold to be held in bank reserves. Ashigbey said the gold must also be certified by the London Bullion Market Association (LBMA). “It is very critical because for the Bank of Ghana to be able to take that gold and put it into its reserves, for example, for any of these banks, it needs to be LBMA certified,” he said. The Ghana Chamber of Mines is working with the Bank of Ghana, the Gold Board, the Ministries of Lands and Natural Resources and Finance, and the Minerals Commission on a plan to supply the Royal Ghana Gold Refinery with gold from large-scale mines. Ashigbey said the refinery was already processing responsibly sourced feedstock from the mines, starting the process toward LBMA certification. He said the plan was to process 30% of stock for about three years and then complete the remaining steps. For ASM gold, he said, traceability and responsible sourcing remain major challenges. To qualify for markets that pay a premium, gold must be traced to its origin and shown to come from a responsibly mined source. Until those conditions are met, Ashigbey said, ASM gold would have to go to markets that do not pay a premium. “Then you don’t get premium from the gold that you produce,” he said. He said Ghana must continue working with large-scale mines while helping ASM operators adopt responsible sourcing practices to strengthen the country’s gold beneficiation efforts.

items.title: Cancer de la prostate au Burkina Faso : Plus de 630 cas de décès enregistré chaque année
items.description: Au Burkina Faso, près de deux décès par jour sont dû au cancer de la prostate selon le mnistre de la santé. À l'occasion de Novembre Bleu 2026, le ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, tire la sonnette d'alarme sur la progression des cancers masculins. Selon les données de GLOBOCAN 2024 citées dans sa déclaration, le cancer de la prostate représente 1 014 nouveaux cas et 631 décès par an au Burkina Faso. Le gouvernement entend renforcer la prévention, le diagnostic précoce et l'accès aux soins. Le cancer de la prostate demeure une préoccupation majeure de santé publique au Burkina Faso. À l'occasion de la campagne Novembre Bleu 2026, consacrée à la sensibilisation sur les cancers masculins, le ministre de la Santé, Dr Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, a appelé les hommes à briser le silence autour de leur santé et à consulter sans attendre l'apparition de complications. Placée sous le thème « Les cancers masculins, un véritable fléau, parlons-en », cette édition met particulièrement l'accent sur les cancers de la prostate et des testicules, ainsi que sur la nécessité d'améliorer la prévention et la prise en charge des maladies touchant les hommes. Dans sa déclaration, le ministre s'appuie sur les données de GLOBOCAN 2024 pour souligner l'ampleur du problème. Avec 1 014 nouveaux cas annuels, soit 20,5 % de l'ensemble des nouveaux cancers masculins, le cancer de la prostate occupe la première place parmi les cancers touchant les hommes au Burkina Faso. Il serait également responsable de 631 décès chaque année, soit près de deux décès par jour. Derrière ces statistiques se trouvent des familles confrontées à des difficultés médicales, psychologiques, sociales et financières. Pour les autorités sanitaires, le diagnostic tardif constitue l'un des principaux obstacles à une prise en charge efficace. Des investissements pour améliorer la prise en charge Face à cette situation, le gouvernement affirme poursuivre le renforcement des capacités nationales de lutte contre le cancer. Parmi les mesures mises en avant figurent la mise en place d'un Programme national de lutte contre le cancer et l'adoption du décret n° 2023-0641 du 1er juin 2023, portant gratuité de la radiothérapie dans le traitement de certains cancers fréquents, notamment celui de la prostate. Le ministre évoque également la construction, l'équipement et la mise en fonctionnement de trois centres de radiothérapie, dont deux à Ouagadougou et un à Bobo-Dioulasso. À ces infrastructures s'ajoutent le recrutement et la formation de spécialistes en urologie, notamment dans le cadre de l'Initiative présidentielle 1000 x 5, ainsi que l'élaboration d'un protocole national de prise en charge du cancer de la prostate. Un groupe de travail a par ailleurs été mis en place pour renforcer la concertation entre les différents acteurs intervenant dans la lutte contre les cancers urologiques. Subvention des médicaments et équipement médical en perspective Malgré ces acquis annoncés, les autorités reconnaissent que plusieurs défis restent à relever. Le département de la Santé prévoit notamment de travailler à la subvention des médicaments utilisés dans le traitement du cancer de la prostate. L'installation d'un appareil de tomographie par émission de positons couplée au scanner (TEP-Scanner) figure également parmi les perspectives annoncées. Le gouvernement entend aussi renforcer la formation des ressources humaines spécialisées, améliorer la communication sur les cancers de la prostate et de la vessie, et élaborer des directives nationales pour favoriser leur prévention et leur détection précoce. Les hommes appelés à consulter sans attendre Au-delà des investissements médicaux, le ministre insiste sur la nécessité de changer les comportements. La peur, la gêne et les préjugés continuent, selon lui, d'éloigner certains hommes des structures sanitaires. Il encourage particulièrement les hommes de 50 ans et plus à discuter avec un professionnel de santé des modalités de dépistage du cancer de la prostate, notamment à travers le dosage de l'antigène prostatique spécifique (PSA) et le toucher rectal, en fonction de leur situation individuelle. Les personnes ayant des antécédents familiaux de cancer de la prostate sont invitées à aborder cette question plus tôt avec un professionnel de santé. Les difficultés à uriner, les envies fréquentes d'uriner, la présence de sang dans les urines ou l'impossibilité d'uriner sont également des signes qui nécessitent une consultation médicale rapide. Le ministre appelle enfin les professionnels de santé, les médias, les leaders coutumiers et religieux, les associations et les organisations de la société civile à participer activement à la sensibilisation. Briser les tabous pour sauver des vies Au Burkina Faso, la campagne Novembre Bleu ne se limite donc pas à une opération de communication. Elle pose la question de l'accès à l'information, de la consultation précoce et de la disponibilité des soins spécialisés. Derrière chaque cas de cancer, il y a un homme, une famille et parfois des proches qui doivent affronter une longue épreuve. Parler de sa santé, accepter une consultation et s'informer sur les possibilités de dépistage sont autant de démarches qui peuvent contribuer à améliorer les chances de prise en charge. Le message du ministre est clair : la santé masculine ne doit plus être un sujet de silence ou de honte. La prévention et le recours aux professionnels de santé doivent devenir des réflexes. items.title: Ghana @ 70: InLaME CEO questions gains in leadership and institutional development
items.description: As Ghana prepares to mark 70 years of independence, concerns are mounting over whether the country has built the strong institutions and effective leadership needed to deliver sustainable development. Founder and CEO of the Institute of Leadership and Management in Education (InLaME), Nii Armah Addy, says the anniversary must trigger an honest national assessment of Ghana’s governance record rather than become another round of celebrations. He argues that despite decades of self-governance, persistent weaknesses in accountability, education and institutional effectiveness continue to undermine the country’s development ambitions. “As Ghana approaches seventy years of independence, we must ask ourselves some fundamental questions. Have we built the institutions we envisioned at independence? Have we developed the leadership capacity required to sustain our democracy and accelerate national development?” he asked. Leadership and institutional weaknesses Mr Addy says investment in infrastructure and natural resources alone cannot deliver prosperity without capable leadership, accountable public officials and effective institutions. He believes Ghana must strengthen the institutions responsible for translating policies and political commitments into tangible improvements in citizens’ lives. Independence must deliver better living conditions He argues that Ghana’s progress must be measured by improvements in citizens’ living conditions, opportunities and dignity, not simply the number of years since independence. “The strength of every nation lies not only in its natural resources or physical infrastructure, but in the quality of its people, the integrity of its leadership and the effectiveness of its institutions,” he stated. Preparing the next generation Mr Addy also identifies education, innovation and leadership development as critical to preparing young Ghanaians for future challenges. “The Ghana we envision for the next generation must be built on knowledge, innovation, accountability and purposeful leadership. We cannot leave the future to chance,” he added. InLaME to convene national dialogue His comments come ahead of InLaME’s Ghana @ 70 initiative on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at the British Council Auditorium in Accra. Under the theme, “Standing Here, Looking Back to Look into the Future,” the event will bring together policymakers, academics, education professionals and development partners to discuss leadership, governance, education and institutional transformation. Ghana marks 70 years of independence on March 6, 2027.

items.title: Les autorités mauritaniennes ordonnent aux orpailleurs dans le Tiris Zemour d’évacuer les sites situés à 10 km de la frontière
items.description: Le gouverneur du Tiris-Zemour, Idriss Demba Corera, a ordonné mardi aux chercheurs d’or des sites situés à 10 kilomètres de la frontière d’évacuer cette zone dans un délai maximal de deux semaines. Le wali a appelé les orpailleurs à « se conformer à cette décision, à respecter le territoire national et à se conformer aux instructions des autorités compétentes ». Cette déclaration a été faite lors d’une visite sur le terrain qui a couvert plusieurs zones d’exploitation aurifère de la région et qui visait « à sensibiliser les chercheurs d’or sur la nécessité de respecter les règles régissant l’exploitation minière artisanale et de se conformer aux mesures de sécurité ». Le wali a précisé que « la décision d’évacuer les sites d’exploitation situés dans la bande frontalière, à une profondeur de dix kilomètres à l’intérieur du territoire national, vise à renforcer la sécurité des frontières et à permettre aux forces armées d’accomplir leurs missions de protection du territoire national, et à protéger les chercheurs d’or et à les éloigner des zones frontalières », selon l’Agence mauritanienne d’information (officielle). Des prospecteurs des zones proches de la frontière avaient déclaré dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche dernier, lors d’un entretien avec le correspondant de Sahara Media dans la wilaya de Tiris Zemmour, qu’environ 15 obus étaient tombés à l’ouest des sites d’exploration, sans faire de victimes selon ses propos, dans le contexte d’un échange de tirs près du mur de séparation dans le Sahara. Selon les déclarations des chercheurs de pétrole, le Front Polisario a pris pour cible les zones de « Tarf Abdo » et « Tarf Menine », situées à proximité du mur de sable, tandis que l’armée marocaine a riposté en bombardant les zones d’« Akleibat al-Foul » et d’« Oum Arouissine », situées à l’extérieur du mur.

items.title: Troops kill 21 suspected ISWAP fighters in Borno
items.description: … As terrorists kill five, abduct 11 in Askira-Uba By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Troops of the Joint Task Force, North East, Operation HADIN KAI, have neutralised 21 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters and injured 10 others in separate air operations around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area of Borno State. The military operations, conducted between November 16 and 17, 2026, came amid renewed attacks by insurgents in parts of the state. In a separate incident, suspected terrorists on Tuesday invaded Pubaku village in Rumirgo Ward, Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Southern Borno, killing five residents and abducting 11 others, including 10 women. The attackers were also said to have set several residential buildings and shops ablaze, forcing residents to flee into the bush for safety. In a statement issued on Wednesday, Acting Media Information Officer, Headquarters Joint Task Force North East, Operation HADIN KAI, Captain Mohammed Goni, said the military air strikes followed intelligence reports of terrorist movements around Monguno and the South Lake Chad area. He said the first operation was launched after intelligence indicated that ISWAP fighters were advancing towards Monguno. According to him, an unmanned aerial vehicle deployed for surveillance identified the fighters moving along a bush path northeast of Monguno, prompting a precision air strike that neutralised seven insurgents, including members of the group’s Improvised Explosive Device network. Goni said further assessment of the operation showed that ABBA BOMMA, identified as a key IED team expert, was incapacitated, while four other fighters sustained severe injuries. He disclosed that a second operation at Arinna, in the South Lake Chad area, dealt a significant blow to the group’s leadership and operational structure. Among those killed, according to the military, was MALLAM SHARKI, a member of the group’s Shura Council and Amirul Amniya (Provost Commander). Also neutralised was ABU SAAD, identified as the Qaid of Sabon Tumbu, alongside 12 other fighters, while five insurgents sustained severe injuries. Several motorcycles belonging to the terrorists were also destroyed during the operation. Goni said the two operations resulted in the neutralisation of 21 ISWAP fighters and injuries to 10 others, adding that the strikes had weakened the group’s leadership structure, disrupted its IED network and degraded its operational capabilities. He reaffirmed the Theatre Command’s commitment to sustaining military operations against terrorists until lasting peace and normalcy were restored across the North-East. The military also urged residents to continue providing security agencies with credible and timely information. Meanwhile, residents of Pubaku confirmed the attack on their community, saying the assailants operated without resistance before fleeing after killing five people, abducting 11 residents and destroying property. A resident, Yakubu Pubagu, who spoke with our correspondent on Wednesday, described the incident as devastating. “Yes, there was a devastating attack on our community (Pubagu) on Tuesday, where five of our people were killed, 10 women and one man abducted after destroying many houses,” he said. The attack left the community largely deserted as residents fled to nearby bushes for safety. The incident came barely 48 hours after suspected insurgents reportedly fired several mortar rounds targeting the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, former Borno State Governor, Maina Maaji Lawan, and other stakeholders during a political mobilisation visit to Kukawa Local Government Area in support of All Progressives Congress candidates. items.title: Campagne agricole de saison sèche : Dans le Oubri, le ministre Ismaël Sombié accélère les préparatifs de la production
items.description: À Nagréongo, un périmètre agricole de 28 hectares est en cours de préparation. Le ministre d’État a également salué une initiative solidaire visant à développer la production maraîchère au profit des personnes déplacées internes et des populations vulnérables. Les préparatifs de la campagne agricole de saison sèche s’intensifient dans la région du Oubri. Le ministre d’État, ministre de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le commandant Ismaël Sombié, a effectué, le mardi 17 novembre 2026, une visite de terrain pour évaluer l’état d’avancement des aménagements et s’assurer des conditions de démarrage des activités de production. Cette sortie s’inscrit dans le cadre du suivi de la mise en œuvre du plan d’urgence de la campagne non pluvieuse, avec pour objectif d’accélérer l’opérationnalisation des sites agricoles et de renforcer les capacités de production nationale. Première étape de cette tournée : la commune de Nagréongo. Sur place, le ministre d’État a visité un périmètre agricole de 28 hectares dont les travaux de labour sont entièrement achevés. Le site est désormais en phase de préparation pour accueillir différentes cultures maraîchères, notamment la tomate, l’oignon et l’aubergine. Les équipes techniques du ministère sont mobilisées pour accompagner les producteurs dans les différentes étapes de mise en valeur du périmètre. L’objectif est de permettre un démarrage effectif des activités et de faire de cet espace un véritable bassin de production pendant la saison sèche. Une initiative solidaire au profit des personnes déplacées internes La tournée ministérielle s’est poursuivie sur le site du guérisseur traditionnel El Hadj Seydou BIKIENGA. Ce dernier a entrepris, sur fonds d’initiative personnelle, la réalisation de forages destinés à soutenir les activités agricoles en période non pluvieuse. Son projet vise notamment à offrir des possibilités de production aux personnes déplacées internes ainsi qu’aux populations qu’il accueille. Une démarche qui associe activité agricole, solidarité et accompagnement des personnes en situation de vulnérabilité. Saluant cette initiative, le commandant Ismaël Sombié a instruit les services techniques compétents de lui apporter un accompagnement approprié. Cet appui devra concerner l’encadrement des producteurs, l’organisation du travail et surtout la gestion rationnelle de l’eau, indispensable à la pérennité des activités agricoles en saison sèche. Transformer les aménagements en espaces de production À travers cette visite, le ministre d’État entend donner une nouvelle impulsion à la mise en œuvre du plan d’urgence de la campagne non pluvieuse. Il s’agit notamment de veiller à la mobilisation des producteurs, à la mise en exploitation effective des périmètres aménagés et à la valorisation des initiatives locales susceptibles de contribuer à l'augmentation de la production agricole. Dans la région du Oubri, les préparatifs semblent ainsi progresser. Mais au-delà des travaux d'aménagement et des équipements mobilisés, le véritable défi reste celui de la production effective. Pour les populations bénéficiaires, particulièrement les personnes déplacées internes, ces espaces agricoles représentent aussi une possibilité de retrouver une activité génératrice de revenus et de renforcer leur autonomie alimentaire. La réussite de cette campagne dépendra donc de la capacité des différents acteurs à transformer les infrastructures disponibles en exploitations productives et durables. Un enjeu majeur dans la quête de souveraineté alimentaire du Burkina Faso. items.title: Farmers’ quest for quick weed control sustains illegal use of banned agrochemicals — NAFDAC
items.description: …Warns of health risks from chemical residues By Cynthia Alo Farmers’ preference for fast-acting agrochemicals is sustaining the illegal importation and use of banned chemicals in Nigeria, the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has said. The agency said some farmers continued to patronise prohibited products because of their effectiveness in killing weeds within a short period, despite the potential health risks to human life associated with those chemicals. Director, North West Zone, NAFDAC, Dadi Nantim Mullah, disclosed this in an exclusive interview with Vanguard Agrobiz in Lagos. Mullah explained that the increasing demand for food, driven by population growth and the expansion of food businesses, had heightened the need to produce and preserve food on a larger scale, leading to greater reliance on agrochemicals. He said the need to store food for longer periods, particularly as restaurants and other food businesses catered to more consumers, had made preservation increasingly important. According to him, the expansion of farm sizes had also increased farmers’ need for chemicals to support production process. He stated: “Because of explosion in population, people need to have food stored longer than they normally would. “For instance, if before, we can buy tomatoes, cook it and eat same day, but now, we have restaurants wanting to have much more tomatoes to cook for many more people. So, people need to grind it, preserve it, and then reach more people. “That process looks simple, but it requires a lot of efforts which has to be supported by some conventional or unconventional applications. ‘‘The farmer who was using half an acre, but has suddenly expanded to 10 acres, would need increased aid to meet the increased production demand. “So, chemicals came in to help, whether they are pesticides, herbicides, or whatsoever it is that can help to produce more, preserve more.” However, he warned that the increased use of agrochemicals could expose consumers to harmful chemical residues when farmers and other users applied inappropriate products or exceeded prescribed quantities. Mullah specifically identified paraquat-containing products among the banned chemicals still being brought into Nigeria illegally, despite the agency’s prohibition. He said farmers continued to favour the chemical because of its rapid weed-killing effect, with a single application reportedly drying grass within 24 hours. He said: “If you don’t use the correct quantity, or you don’t use the chemical that is appropriate for the type of food that you want to preserve, it will eventually affect the consumer. We have what we call pesticide residues. “Some of them are banned already by NAFDAC, so that we will not use them. I’ll give you an example with paraquat-containing pesticides. “They are brought in. Farmers love that chemical because if you spray it on your farm, within 24 hours grass is dried, but it retains and it causes cancer. And that impact is not good for the health of the consumer.” According to him, NAFDAC banned the chemical about two years ago, but illegal importation has continued because of its demand. He also listed atrazine among chemicals banned by the agency, urging farmers not to select agrochemicals simply because they appear more effective or are being used by other farmers. He said: “NAFDAC banned those type of chemicals two years ago, but people are still bringing them in illegally. “Don’t use any chemical you don’t know what it is meant for. Don’t apply it simply because it looks good, or somebody else used it. Ensure you follow NAFDAC-approved guidelines in using these chemicals to preserve food for the public.” Mullah explained that NAFDAC has maintained daily inspections at borders and facilities to check the importation of prohibited chemicals and ensure that approved agrochemicals are used according to prescribed guidelines. He said: “First, those that are impacting on our health, cancer-causing, NAFDAC has banned, and one of them I mentioned is paraquat. There are others—atrazine and all those ones that have been banned by NAFDAC so that we will not use them in the country. “We conduct inspections at the borders and in facilities to ensure those who are using or importing the ones that are approved, they are using it in appropriate prescribed guidelines.” He added that the agency conducts daily market inspections, withdrawing and destroying products found to be expired or improperly stored. “We go out every day in NAFDAC. Every single day we go out. We mop out the ones we see in the markets or in the stores or sales outlets,” he said. Mullah urged farmers to follow approved guidelines in selecting and applying agrochemicals, stressing that the drive to increase food production and preserve supplies should not compromise food safety and consumers’ health. The post Farmers’ quest for quick weed control sustains illegal use of banned agrochemicals — NAFDAC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Conakry : des centaines de maisons et parcelles sur des bras de mer dans le viseur de la CRIEF à Gbessia Faban
items.description: Screenshot " data-large-file="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/IMG_1894.jpeg?fit=1024%2C691&ssl=1" /> Des villas, des duplex, des bâtiments en construction et des terrains nus figurent dans un inventaire transmis au parquet spécial près la CRIEF (Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières). Selon Mondemedia, qui affirme avoir consulté le document, les investigations portent sur des occupations immobilières présumées irrégulières du domaine public maritime et sur les conditions de délivrance de plusieurs titres d’occupation. La gestion du domaine public maritime en Guinée se retrouve au cœur de nouvelles investigations judiciaires. Le parquet spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF) s’intéresse à plusieurs domaines immobiliers qui seraient implantés sur des bras de mer. Selon les informations rapportées par Mondemedia, qui indique avoir consulté le document de recensement, le procureur spécial près la CRIEF, Alphonse Charles Wright, avait adressé, le 28 septembre 2026, une réquisition N°578/CRIEF/PPS/2026 à la Direction nationale de l’aménagement du territoire et de l’urbanisme (DATU). Cette démarche visait à identifier les domaines concernés et à vérifier leur situation administrative et foncière. En réponse, la DATU a transmis au parquet spécial son rapport de recensement N°6428/DATU/MUHAT/CAP/2026, daté du 20 octobre 2026. Ce document fait état de nombreuses occupations immobilières sur des espaces présentés comme relevant du domaine public maritime. Des occupations immobilières au cœur des soupçons Dans les motifs exposés par le parquet spécial, les terrains recensés seraient situés sur des bras de mer appartenant au domaine public maritime. Ces espaces ne pourraient donc faire l’objet d’une appropriation privée ou d’une cession à des fins personnelles, notamment pour la construction d’habitations et la réalisation de projets immobiliers. Le parquet soulève également des interrogations sur la régularité de certaines opérations de lotissement et de validation de plans d’aménagement. Des cadres du ministère de l’Urbanisme, de l’Habitat et de l’Aménagement du territoire sont notamment mis en cause dans le dossier pour avoir procédé, selon les éléments de la procédure, à la validation présumée irrégulière de certains plans, en violation du décret D/2023/0190/PRG/CNRD/SGG du 19 août 2023 portant réglementation des opérations de lotissement en République de Guinée. Le rôle de responsables communaux chargés de l’urbanisme, de l’habitat et de l’aménagement du territoire est également évoqué, de même que celui de certains présidents de conseils de quartier qui auraient participé à la délivrance de titres d’occupation. Des villas, des duplex et des centaines de parcelles recensés L’inventaire annexé au rapport de la DATU révèle une diversité de situations immobilières. Il fait état de parcelles attribuées à des particuliers, sur lesquelles sont recensés des terrains nus, des espaces clôturés, des fondations, des soubassements, des villas achevées, des duplex ainsi que des bâtiments à plusieurs niveaux. Selon Mondemedia, plusieurs personnes figurent dans cet inventaire, notamment Ismaël Nidal Diabaté, Kalil Oularé, Mamadi Kaba, Mohamed Diallo, Mathieu Tolno, Mory Kaba, Hassan Nabé et Mamadou Mountaga Bah. Certains occupants seraient détenteurs de plusieurs parcelles et disposeraient de documents tels que des attestations de donation, des attestations de cession ou des plans de masse. Le recensement mentionne également des parcelles attribuées à des personnes non identifiées. Ces éléments soulèvent des questions sur les conditions dans lesquelles ces terrains ont été lotis, attribués et occupés, mais aussi sur la responsabilité des différentes autorités administratives et locales intervenues dans ces opérations. Il convient toutefois de préciser que la présence d’un nom dans le rapport de recensement ne constitue pas, à elle seule, une preuve de culpabilité ni ne signifie que la personne concernée fait l’objet de poursuites judiciaires. Les responsabilités individuelles restent à établir dans le cadre de la procédure. L’enjeu de cette affaire est désormais de déterminer comment des propriétés immobilières ont pu être constituées sur des espaces relevant potentiellement du domaine public maritime et d’établir les responsabilités éventuelles dans la chaîne de lotissement et de délivrance des titres d’occupation. Une synthèse de Yaya Barry L’article Conakry : des centaines de maisons et parcelles sur des bras de mer dans le viseur de la CRIEF à Gbessia Faban est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata retires aged 38
items.description: Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement at 38. Mata, who made 41 international appearances, was part of the Spain squad that won the 2010 World Cup, and he helped his country win the European Championship two years later, scoring in the 4-0 final win over Italy. A former Real Madrid youth player, he joined Valencia in 2007 before a move to Chelsea in August 2011, where he won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup. Mata moved to Manchester United in January 2014 and helped them win the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup before leaving in 2022. He went on to have spells at Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory. “Football will never leave my life,” said Mata. “There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development. “I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer.” Mata was Chelsea’s player of the year in both full seasons he was at Stamford Bridge. He made 82 league appearances for the club, scoring 18 goals. “What a player,” Chelsea posted on social media. At Manchester United, he scored 51 goals in 285 outings before leaving after his contract expired. “Congratulations on a fantastic career, Juan! Everyone at United wishes you all the best in your next steps,” said United statement., external
