Gouvernance locale: Le Bureau du Citoyen officiellement installé à Agbodrafo
items.description: Aného, 18 nov. (ATOP) – Le Bureau du citoyen (BDC), instance indépendante d’écoute, de médiation et d’orientation, a été officiellement installé, le mardi 17 novembre à Agbodrafo, au palais royal du chef canton . Le mandat des membres est fixé à trois ans, renouvelable trois fois. Une durée qui inscrit cette mission dans la continuité et permet d’envisager un accompagnement durable des préoccupations citoyennes. La cérémonie s’est déroulée au palais royal du chef canton d’Agbodrafo, en présence des chefs de villages et des membres des Comités villageois de développement (CVD) de l’ensemble du ressort territorial. Ce cadre permanent vise à promouvoir la transparence dans la gestion des affaires publiques et à encourager l’implication active des populations dans le développement socio-économique de la commune. Sur le plan organisationnel, le Bureau du Citoyen dispose d’un siège et est placé sous l’autorité hiérarchique du maire. Il est dirigé par un coordonnateur, Agbekoué Koffi, assisté d’une rapporteuse, Mme Bocna Rebécala. L’équipe ainsi mise en place aura la responsabilité d’assurer le fonctionnement de cette structure et de faciliter les échanges entre les citoyens et les instances communales. Avec l’installation de ce Bureau du Citoyen, la commune Lacs 3 se dote ainsi d’un nouvel instrument de dialogue et de participation à la gouvernance locale. Le défi sera désormais de faire vivre cette structure au quotidien, en garantissant son accessibilité, son écoute et sa capacité à assurer le relais des préoccupations des populations auprès des autorités compétentes. Le Bureau du Citoyen est un organe indépendant mis en place pour faciliter le dialogue entre les autorités communales et les populations. Il constitue un espace où chaque citoyen peut exprimer ses préoccupations, formuler des propositions, solliciter des orientations ou faire part de ses difficultés en rapport avec la gestion des affaires locales. ATOP/AAK/SED

items.title: 'He who claims equity must come with clean hands': Asif hits back at Bilawal
items.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif joined others from the ruling PML-N on Wednesday in responding to PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari following the latter’s hard-hitting speech over several issues, including new provinces, constitutional tweaks and treatment of the opposition. “He who claims equity must come with clean hands,” Asif reminded Bilawal in a post on X, as the wrangling between coalition partners PML-N and PPP appeared to deepen. The exchange has particularly heated up after Bilawal delivered a no-holds-barred speech the previous day that covered the question of new provinces. The Bhutto scion also expressed support for several opposition demands and questioned past decisions and actions taken by the ruling coalition. Bilawal referred to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s recommendation of holding a referendum to decide on the creation of new administrative units and said: “In our history, a referendum has always been carried out for an undemocratic act and never a democratic one.” The PPP chairperson also remarked that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse” — seemingly reacting to Naqvi’s statement in July that the current “system” of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”. Asif began his response to Bilawal by addressing this matter. He said: “No system can reset without public support. If you are talking about a system collapse, then all of us, as people connected to this system, must also take stock of our responsibilities. The defence minister also appeared to throw his weight behind the proposal for holding a referendum on new provinces as he said that there would surely be a debate on “system reset” in Parliament, but the public too could not be “deprived of its fundamental right”. “The pinnacle of legitimacy would be reached if the public opinion is also taken into account along with that of Parliament.” Seemingly reacting to Bilawal’s support for the release of incarcerated former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan and other demands by the opposition, Asif added: “Holding politicians accountable in this country is nothing new, and no politician exempt from accountability.” He mentioned that the PPP had been in power in Sindh for 18 years. “Sindh has turned into paradise. The world admires the condition of Karachi,” he said, seemingly taking a jibe at the PPP, which is often criticised over the lack of development in Sindh. Asif then said Bilawal and his party had been a “partner of the PML-N in the business of government since 2022. You get the profit and the PML-N and Pakistan suffer loss”. “He who claims equity must come with clean hands,” Asif continued. “This is a centuries-old maxim of equity. Are your hands clean? Do you have the right to lecture or threaten?” The defence minister said, “We have just one objective: to change the lives of the people of Pakistan so that ordinary people can live with dignity. Make public participation in governance a reality … Do not confine the people’s rights to the pages of the Constitution.” He said after achievements on diplomatic and military fronts, now the “fight is for devolving governance to grassroots, in which public opinion and Parliament’s role are entirely democratic and constitutional. Governance is not anyone’s monopoly; Allah has granted this right to 250 million people.” ‘Sins are not washed away in this manner’ Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also reacted to Bilawal’s speech, saying that while the Bhutto scion presented himself as a “champion” of the Constitution and democracy, he was well versed only in theory on the subject and, in practice, his performance was “zero”. He said Bilawal’s remarks the previous day were akin to picking and choosing certain provisions of the Constitution that suited him and disregarding others as unconstitutional. Chaudhry said the PPP was currently in power in three provinces, as well as Gilgit-Baltistan. The president and Senate chairperson were also from the PPP, he further pointed out, commenting: “And then you give the impression as if you are the opposition leader, as if you are not associated with the government in any way.” He also appeared to be criticising the PPP for being in favour of the creation of a south Punjab province and opposing the carving out of new administrative units in Sindh. “So you call for breaking an administrative unit where governance is good and those where governance is bad should be left?” The minister said Bilawal had also remarked that the 27th Amendment had been passed “with brute majority”. “Were the votes cast the same way for the 1973 Constitution, or the 18th Amendment? Or do you believe that after voting like this, you can hold a press conference, act innocent and dissociate yourself, [as if] you did not realise [what was happening]. “Then you may also vote for the legislation for administrative units and later hold such a press conference saying it was due to force. “Sins are not washed away in this manner. You cannot dissociate yourself in this manner,” he added. “Everyone remembers that speech of yours in the National Assembly in which you said that a constitutional court was Quaid-i-Azam’s dream,” Chaudhry recalled. “Then you referenced your mother’s speeches saying she wanted to create a constitutional court, and then you said — ‘This is our legacy. Carrying forward our legacy, today we have done the work that we had been wanting to do for the past 50 years’ — meaning the PPP wanted to do it. You took credit for the entire amendment, and today you’re saying that votes were cast forcibly.” Chaudhry claimed Bilawal and his party opposed creation of new provinces in order to maintain control over resources. He referred to the PPP chairperson’s statement that if Sindh were to be divided, there could be bloodshed and called it “regrettable”. “The question is: does casting a vote cause blood to flow, or does it stop bloodshed? You always say the decision should come through the ballot, not the bullet. So when did you start fearing the vote?” Chaudhry said. “During 17 years of [PPP] rule, your governance has drained the blood of the people of Sindh. First check whether any blood is even left in them or not,” Chaudhry quipped. According to the state minister, Bilawal merely wanted to accept “half the constitution” while claiming the rest as wrongly framed. “In other words, are you calling the very Constitution you framed unconstitutional?” he asked. “Democracy is not merely about delivering speeches, interpreting or explaining articles of the Constitution to show these are the rights of the people. Democracy also involves performance. Democracy also entails governance,” he added. In response to Bilawal’s remarks on the 27th Amendment, Chaudhry said such amendments to the Constitution had been made over time to improve governance and held that the 27 amendments so far had also been made with that objective. ‘PPP crushed the move’ Separately, Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, whose party had also been demanding the creation of new administrative units in the country, questioned why the PPP was worried over the creation of new provinces if its performance in the government had been good. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he painted a derelict picture of Sindh and asserted that power should be devolved to provinces. He said the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan had tried to get this done through the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments, “but the PPP crushed” the move. ‘If govt lacks legitimacy, Zardari should resign’ Speaking to media in Islamabad, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman called on the PPP chairman to review his party’s history before opposing the creation of new provinces. Rehman also challenged Bilawal to present the Form-45s of the party’s seven National Assembly seats from Karachi. The JI chief further stated that the PPP chairman should recall his party’s role in the ethnic unrest triggered by the 1972 language bill in Sindh before warning of bloodshed over the creation of new provinces. He maintained that administrative provinces should be created through a constitutional process. The JI chief said that his party was in support of creation of fresh administrative units, provided it was done so constitutionally. Rehman added that while the PPP claimed the incumbent government was illegitimate, President Asif Ali Zardari secured his office with the support of the same government. “If the government lacks legitimacy, Zardari should resign,” he said. Rehman also questioned Bilawal’s sympathy for the PTI, asking why the PPP facilitated the PTI government’s removal in the past. He also recalled that President Zardari had signed the order to impose governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel and Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
items.description: The body overseeing US President Donald Trump’s plan to end the Gaza war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse. The 12-page Board of Peace report, seen by Reuters , is the body’s second to the United Nations Security Council since the US-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then. The board, established and headed by Trump , is expected to present the report’s findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November. “The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process,” the report said, warning that “a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely.” In Gaza, witnesses said Israeli tanks advanced onto the main Salahudeen road, west of the Yellow Line that marks the boundary of the two-thirds of the Gaza Strip still under Israeli control despite a ceasefire that has lasted more than a year. An Israeli airstrike near the army raid killed one person, Palestinian medics said. The medics said separate Israeli airstrikes had killed two other people earlier in the day in Deir al-Balah and Gaza City. An Israeli military spokesperson claimed the military was carrying out an operation targeting “Hamas infrastructure” west of the Yellow Line in central Gaza and that it had struck a fighter in southern Gaza earlier on Wednesday. The spokesperson had no immediate comment on other strikes. Peace plan stalled While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year. Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected the roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas is dismantled. Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza , while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops. “Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas’ agreement to the roadmap to the test,” the report said. “Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble.” Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as “pure disinformation”, accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to continue its aggression in Gaza. The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and a spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Israeli ‘absence of decisions’ Gaza’s population of more than 2 million Palestinians lives confined to around a third of the coastal territory, mostly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings, under the control of Hamas fighters. Israel occupies two-thirds of Gaza that has been largely razed and depopulated. The report criticised Israel’s government for an “absence of decisions” on arrangements to train and deploy a civilian Palestinian police force to replace Hamas as Gaza’s law enforcement authority. It said this was impeding the full implementation of the plan. It said restrictions imposed by Israel on supplies and equipment, alongside funding shortfalls, had hindered the ability of Gazans to prepare for and respond to seasonal flooding. Heavy rain inundated displacement camps last week across Gaza and more rain is expected later this month. Hamas, for its part, was collecting taxes on goods entering Gaza that were impacting the availability of basic commodities, the report said. The Board of Peace was established by Trump to oversee his ambitious plan to end the war that Israel launched in response to Hamas-led attacks from Gaza in October 2023. Around 1,200 people were killed in Israel in the 2023 Hamas attacks, while the Israeli assault on Gaza has since killed 74,000 Palestinians. More than 1,600 Palestinians, including many civilians, and five Israeli soldiers have been killed in Gaza since the US-mediated ceasefire was struck in October 2025. Trump’s plan received strong international backing, though the board itself has been met with scepticism from many of Washington’s Western allies. Netanyahu’s right-wing coalition government remains in power in Israel in a caretaker capacity despite losing its majority in an inconclusive election last month. On Wednesday, Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel would not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas was dismantled and Gaza was demilitarised.

items.title: AVE : Les élèves d’Assahoun sensibilisés à la culture de la tolérance
items.description: Kévé, 18 nov. (ATOP) – Les élèves du lycée d’Assahoun ont été sensibilisés à la tolérance, le mardi 17 novembre dans la localité, à l’occasion de la célébration de la journée internationale de la tolérance. Placée sous le thème « Faisons des réseaux sociaux, un espace de tolérance », cette activité est initiée par le ministère en charge des Droits humains, à travers la direction de la Formation civique. Elle vise à susciter une prise de conscience collective sur la nécessité de promouvoir le respect et le vivre-ensemble, notamment dans les espaces numériques. Il s’agit de promouvoir l’acceptation des différences à travers les actes, les comportements et les paroles, afin de contribuer à la construction d’une société plus juste et pacifique. Les échanges ont porté sur les comportements répréhensibles sur Internet, notamment la diffusion de fausses informations, les atteintes à la vie privée, le cyberharcèlement, les propos haineux et la piraterie informatique. Le formateur, Daniel Agano, s’est servi des images d’illustration des actes d’intolérance sur des bâches pour toucher toutes les formes d’intolérance en cours dans les sociétés. Il a rappelé que la journée internationale pour la tolérance a été instituée par une déclaration de principes des États membres de l’UNESCO depuis le 16 novembre 1995. Elle vise, poursuit le formateur, à contribuer à l’instauration du respect et de l’appréciation de la richesse et de la diversité des cultures du monde. « Les nombreux conflits qui déchirent le monde trouvent leur origine dans l’intolérance religieuse, le genre, les idées, le rang social, l’opinion politique. Il fallait trouver un moyen pour arrêter cette attitude qui compromettait le vivre-ensemble », a expliqué M. Agano. Le représentant de la direction de la Formation civique, M. Tchakpala Olivier, a déclaré que « cette journée est une occasion de promouvoir la tolérance, une condition sine qua non au vivre ensemble ». Il a fait savoir que les actes d’intolérance sont aujourd’hui transposés sur les réseaux sociaux, et c’est l’occasion d’attirer l’attention des jeunes sur les actes inciviques qui se développent sur ces réseaux. Le proviseur du lycée d’Assahoun, Vignon Kokou, a invité les élèves à une bonne utilisation des réseaux sociaux pour préserver la cohésion sociale. ATOP/HKM/MD/BV

items.title: Bas-mono : le préfet à la rencontre des forces vives de sa juridiction
items.description: Afagnagan, 18 nov. (ATOP) – Le préfet de Bas-Mono, Colonel Akagna Kodjo a achevé le mardi 17 novembre à Kpétsou, dans la commune Bas-Mono1, sa tournée de prise de contact et d’information avec les populations des différents cantons de sa juridiction. Démarrée le 11 novembre dernier, cette démarche s’inscrit dans la dynamique de renforcement des liens de collaboration entre l’administration préfectorale et les communautés à la base. Ce périple a conduit le préfet et sa délégation à Afagnan-Gbléta, Afagnagan, Attitogon, Hompou, Agbétiko, Agome-Glozou, et puis Kpétsou. Il lui a permis de se faire connaitre des populations, de s’imprégner des réalités du terrain et d’écouter les préoccupations de ses administrés. Le préfet a saisi l’occasion pour partager sa vision pour le développement du milieu avec les populations. Dans chaque localité visitée, le préfet a échangé avec les chefs traditionnels, les leaders communautaires, les responsables des comités de développement à la base (CDQ, CVD et CCD). Il a entretenu ses auditoires sur le développement local, l’unité et le respect mutuel. Il a insisté sur la sécurité des personnes et des biens, la lutte contre l’extrémisme violent en invitant les populations à signaler toute personne étrangère aux autorités compétentes. Le représentant du pouvoir central a rassuré ses administrés de sa disponibilité à travailler avec tous les acteurs pour le développement de la préfecture tout en conviant ses interlocuteurs à la participation aux travaux communautaires, à plus de collaboration avec l’administration. Les chefs des cantons et les populations ont salué la démarche du préfet et évoqué plusieurs préoccupations, notamment l’état des pistes rurales, l’accès à l’eau potable, à la santé, l’éducation, ainsi que l’accompagnement des activités agricoles. Elles se sont engagées à l’accompagner pour la réussite de sa mission. ATOP/DK/AR/BV

items.title: 'It set a positive tone': Xi's airport greeting for Trump breaks decades-long precedent
items.description: Xi Jinping’s personal welcome to US President Donald Trump at Shenzhen airport on Wednesday for a summit made him China’s first paramount leader in decades to greet a foreign counterpart on arrival. After Air Force One touched down, Trump descended to the red carpet, where President Xi himself was waiting to greet him. The men shared a brief hug, before walking together to their cars beside a crowd of cheering performers waving pom-poms. It stood out among other world leaders’ arrivals in Shenzhen this week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting, where Xi, Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin will hold historic three-way talks on Thursday. Putin, who arrived in the early hours of Wednesday, was met by Xi’s right-hand man Cai Qi. But Trump’s personal welcome is believed to be the first by a paramount leader in China in decades — and marks an upgrade to his high-profile summit trip to Beijing in May, when Vice President Han Zheng was there to meet him. Ryan Hass, director of the John L. Thornton China Center at the Brookings Institution, said Trump was “visibly delighted by Xi’s gesture”. “Given Beijing’s overriding objective of extending the fragile calm in the US-China relationship for as long as possible, Xi will look for opportunities to extend courtesy and respect to Trump during his visit, like he did in greeting Trump on the tarmac upon arrival,” Hass told AFP . “It set a positive tone for Trump’s visit, marking a contrast from the swirl of news around the Jensen Huang scandal that preceded Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen.” Huang last week resigned as CEO of US artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia after admitting to an affair, reportedly with a woman some US officials suspect to be a Chinese spy . Xi’s warm greeting of Trump was also reciprocal. When Xi travelled to the US in May, the US leader also met him on arrival, reportedly the first American president in decades to do so, if visits from the Pope are not included. Xi told Trump on the tarmac on Wednesday that during his state visit to the United States, the “presidential couple came to the airport in person and hosted a grand welcome ceremony”, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua . Xi also noted that “China is a nation with a tradition of courtesy that values reciprocating goodwill”, the Xinhua report said. Although several other leaders arriving in Shenzhen for the Apec summit got cheering crowds or bouquets of flowers, one arrival stood out for its relative lack of ceremony. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was greeted not by a top minister, but by military guards and a woman whom Japanese media named as the Chinese foreign ministry’s ambassador of protocol. Long-frosty ties between the countries have worsened since Takaichi suggested last year that Japan could intervene militarily in any conflict over Taiwan, the democratic island Beijing claims as its territory. Meanwhile Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum travelled on a commercial flight, as she often does as part of an austerity policy.

items.title: Oti/Artisanat : La CPM adopte son budget prévisionnel de 2027
items.description: Mango, 18 nov. (ATOP) – La Chambre préfectorale des métiers (CPM) de l’Oti a tenu son assemblée générale ordinaire, le lundi 16 novembre à Mango, dans la commune Oti 1. Les travaux ont porté notamment sur la présentation du budget prévisionnel 2027 et des activités programmées pour le prochain exercice. La rencontre est initiée par le nouveau bureau exécutif élu en août dernier. Elle vise à rendre compte aux délégués des huit cantons de la préfecture des activités réalisées et à venir, ainsi qu’à échanger sur les difficultés du secteur artisanal et les pistes de solutions. Le budget prévisionnel présenté fait état de recettes estimées à 5.930.000 F CFA, provenant notamment de la vente de fiches de contrat, de l’établissement des cartes professionnelles et d’apprentissage, ainsi que de la subvention de l’État. Les dépenses sont évaluées à 4.255.000 F CFA et concernent, entre autres, l’acquisition de matériel informatique et de fournitures de bureau, les charges salariales, les formations, les missions et les œuvres sociales. Au titre des activités de 2027 figurent des sensibilisations sur le rôle des chambres de métiers et l’importance de la carte professionnelle, des formations sur l’hygiène, la qualité et la sécurité au travail, des opérations de reboisement, le recensement des entrepreneurs, la réhabilitation du bar-restaurant du centre des artisans, ainsi que des expositions et foires de produits locaux. Des actions en faveur de l’inclusion des personnes en situation de handicap et des rencontres avec les partenaires sont également prévues. Les délégués ont formulé des doléances, notamment la réduction des frais d’établissement des cartes professionnelles et d’apprentissage. L’adjoint au maire de Oti 1, Dantoukou Bouraima, a salué la tenue de cette assemblée, soulignant le rôle du secteur artisanal dans l’économie nationale. Il a réaffirmé la disponibilité de la commune à accompagner la CPM dans ses activités. Le président régional de la Chambre des métiers des Savanes, Damesonon Sambiani, a exhorté les artisans à œuvrer pour la modernisation des ateliers, la qualification des apprentis et un meilleur accès aux financements et aux marchés publics. Le président de la CPM-Oti, Lanzaré Soulemane, a appelé les artisans à la solidarité et à la discipline pour dynamiser un secteur créateur de richesses et d’emplois. Il a rassuré les délégués que leurs doléances seront transmises aux autorités compétentes et réaffirmé l’engagement de son bureau à promouvoir l’artisanat dans la préfecture. ATOP/TT/JK/SED

items.title: Université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo: Le camarade Souleymane Simporé obtient le grade de docteur
items.description: Le camarade Souleymane Simporé a soutenu sa thèse de doctorat unique en Lettres modernes, le jeudi 12 novembre 2026, dans la salle de réunion des écoles doctorales de l’université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo sur le thème : « Approche éco-étho-sémiotique des innovations environnementales au Burkina Faso : entre éco-formation, non formelle et changement de comportements ». Après avoir jugé le travail recevable, le jury lui a attribué la mention très honorable à l’issue de la soutenance. La mention très honorable a été attribuée au ‘’désormais’’ docteur Souleymane Simporé à l’issue de la soutenance de sa thèse de doctorat unique en Lettres modernes, le jeudi 12 novembre 2026, à l’université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo sur le thème : « Approche éco-étho-sémiotique des innovations environnementales au Burkina Faso : entre éco-formation, non formelle et changement de comportements ». Selon le président du jury, Josph Paré, professeur titulaire à l’université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo, le travail soumis par le camarade Souleymane Simporé dans le cadre de l’obtention du grade de docteur à l’attention du jury a été bien apprécié par l’ensemble du Jury. « La thèse fournit de nombreuses informations qui mettent en relief des enjeux théoriques très importants en matière de formation, d’éco-formation et de transformation des comportements. Le choix orienté vers la sémiotique permet sans aucun doute de voir comment cet outil d’analyse des signes et des comportements au sein d’une société permet de mesurer l’ampleur des changements et la manière dont les innovations peuvent s’insérer dans une société, au sein d’un groupe donné. L’approche prend en considération l’ensemble des zones de production de notre pays. On se rend compte qu’en dépit de la différenciation des zones, les communautés s’approprient un certain nombre d’innovations et de transformations en vue de permettre à ces sociétés d’avancer. C’est un travail de portée scientifique », a-t-il précisé. Le professeur des écoles, Souleymane Simporé (milieu), obtient le grade de docteur avec la mention très honorable. Le directeur de thèse, le maître de conférences Kpanyawne Somda Thadée Balouhib a surtout apprécié la méthode de travail de l’impétrant. Il est parti de la littérature pour aboutir sur un terrain scientifique. Selon lui, les littéraires ne sont pas que des littéraires, ils construisent surtout des humains, ils fabriquent des outils, mais des outils humains. « Le camarade Souleymane Simporé a développé les comportements et les comportements relèvent des sciences humaines qui sont en elles-mêmes la conscience des autres sciences. Si les humains avaient intégré les formations des littéraires, on n’allait pas voir aujourd’hui, un frère prendre une arme contre un autre frère. La formation humaine est une tâche dévolue aux Hommes des sciences humaines. N’oublions pas que Science sans conscience n’est que ruine de l’âme », a-t-il ajouté. Tout heureux, docteur Souleymane Simporé a précisé que son étude propose une approche éco-étho-sémiotique comme cadre d’analyse des innovations environnementales au Burkina Faso, notamment en milieu paysan. Selon lui, le défi est d’articuler la science du développement avec les savoirs endogènes et l’imaginaire burkinabè pour promouvoir l’écocitoyenneté ». Il faut préciser que le travail de recherche de l’impétrant a abouti à des résultats exploitables dans le domaine de la construction de notre société . « Dans nos établissements scolaires par exemple, le jardin scolaire est un cadre d’éco-formation. Contrairement à ce qu’on croit, le jardin scolaire ne doit pas se limiter à la fourniture de condiments à la cantine scolaire. Non, son importance va au-delà. Il est un cadre d’éco-formation qui peut amener les paysans à contribuer d’une manière durable à concrétiser les formations formelles reçues dans les salles de classe », a affirmé docteur Souleymane Simporé. L’impétrant est présentement en exercice dans la région des Koulsé en tant que professeur des écoles. Adama de Maliki malikadams020@gmail.com

(ATOP) – Les membres et sympathisants de la Chambre préfectorale des métiers (CPM) de Cinkassé ont tenu, le mardi 17 novembre à Cinkassé, leur assemblée générale ordinaire, consacrée au bilan des activités et à la planification des actions futures de leur institution. Cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre du pilotage des activités de la chambre et se tient conformément aux textes régissant les chambres de métiers. Elle a permis aux participants d’échanger sur les stratégies visant à améliorer le secteur de l’artisanat dans la préfecture. Les acteurs ont validé le Plan d’action opérationnel (PAO) 2027 de la chambre et adopté son budget prévisionnel. Ce plan prévoit notamment des actions en faveur de la modernisation des ateliers, du renforcement des compétences et de la valorisation du savoir-faire des artisans. D’un montant de 12.521.200 F CFA, le budget prévisionnel sera consacré à la mise en œuvre d’activités concrètes susceptibles de produire des impacts positifs sur le terrain. Le préfet de Cinkassé, colonel Yanani Tiékabe, a souligné l’importance du secteur de l’artisanat dans l’économie nationale. Il a invité les artisans à faire preuve de professionnalisme et à promouvoir l’innovation dans leurs productions. Le secrétaire général de la Chambre régionale des métiers des Savanes, Kassou Adjéoda, et le président de la CPM de Cinkassé, Kariyiaré Nibembane, ont exhorté les participants à privilégier des débats constructifs, afin de faire de la chambre un modèle de réussite et d’innovation. items.title: Philippine Police Detain Hundreds Protesting Trump Visit
items.description: Click to expand Image Protesters attempt to march to the ASEAN Summit venue in Manila but are stopped by hundreds of police officers, November 17, 2026. © 2026 Lian Buan/Human Rights Watch Police in the Philippines arrested and detained at least 245 people protesting the visit of US President Donald Trump to Manila for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit. Protests in Manila started on November 15 opposing the Philippine government’s plan to build a technology manufacturing hub in Capas, Tarlac province, under the US government’s “Pax Silica” initiative. The construction will displace hundreds of Indigenous people and small farmers from their homes and farmlands. An estimated 6,000 people joined the protests despite police efforts to contain demonstrations by banning them everywhere except in “freedom parks” – designated areas where rallies can be held without a permit. Yet police arrested 236 people on the outskirts of Metro Manila who were traveling from the Southern Tagalog region to the main protest site. Among those detained were 29 farmers including members of the Indigenous Mangyan tribe, 19 journalists, 9 environmental defenders, and 6 human rights workers. Ephraim Cortez of the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers said 19 children were detained. “This is the largest mass arrest we’ve seen under [President] Marcos,” protest leader Renato Reyes told Human Rights Watch. “Our whole delegation was arrested and taken to a police camp where lawyers were not given immediate access.” Detainees are being held inside a police camp in a hall with poor ventilation, insufficient drinking water, and inadequate restroom facilities, according to activists and lawyers. The protesters have been detained for three days without charge. Lawyers representing them expressed concern that they could face criminal charges of illegal assembly, alarms and scandals, and disobedience to authority. Police detained without charge another nine protesters at the main protest site on November 15 for attempting to march to the ASEAN summit venue. News footage shows police officers slapping and kicking a protester on the ground. International human rights law protects the right to peaceful assembly. Law enforcement may not carry out indiscriminate mass arrests even if a protest violates local laws or becomes disorderly. Arrests need to be based on individualized grounds and comply with the requirements of legality, necessity, and proportionality. Police can arrest people responsible for specific unlawful conduct but not just for taking part in a protest. All those arbitrarily detained for exercising their basic rights should be immediately released.

items.title: Pour échapper aux régulations, Palmer Luckey veut délocaliser des activités stratégiques sur une plateforme en mer
items.description: Dans la nuit du mardi 17 au mercredi 18 novembre, Palmer Luckey, le cofondateur de l’entreprise américaine de défense Anduril, a annoncé travailler depuis plus de dix ans à la création d’une plateforme artificielle en mer baptisée « SLAB ». Selon Luckey, l’objectif est d’échapper aux lois des États et des collectivités locales qui, selon lui, entravent des industries comme la transformation des métaux, la recherche et les traitements médicaux, le dessalement, le raffinage du pétrole ou le génie chimique. SLAB n’est pas un projet isolé : le seasteading , un mouvement qui œuvre pour l’émergence de communautés autonomes en mer, en tirant profit de l’absence de souveraineté des États dans les eaux internationales, a connu une certaine popularité dans les cercles libertariens dans les années 2000 et 2010. Le mouvement est lié au Seasteading Institute, une organisation créée en 2008 par Wayne Gramlich et Patri Friedman, le petit-fils de l’économiste Milton Friedman, avec le soutien financier de Peter Thiel. L’idée a connu une résurgence au début des années 2020 sous une autre forme, celle de « l’État-réseau » ( network state ), sous l’impulsion de l’entrepreneur Balaji Srinivasan, qui a rejoint la firme de capital-risque Andreessen Horowitz en 2013 avant de devenir directeur technique de la plateforme d’échange de cryptomonnaies Coinbase en 2018, et qui figure parmi les premiers investisseurs d’Anduril. Selling Oculus to Facebook in 2014 gave me money for helicopter flight lessons and developing a seastead called SLAB with a 1,000 year design life. The goal was to be cheaper than land and absent state/local laws that cripple critical American industries like metal processing,… pic.twitter.com/aJkd0eOgLF — Palmer Luckey (@PalmerLuckey) November 18, 2026 Luckey présente SLAB comme une étape vers son « objectif de faire revivre la destinée manifeste et l’expansion vers l’Ouest ». Il ajoute : « À une époque où la plupart des adeptes du seasteading voulaient fuir les États-Unis et fumer de l’herbe, c’était le seul projet explicitement conçu pour rendre l’Amérique plus forte, une soupape de sécurité face à des règles et réglementations mal pensées ou dépassées ». Luckey dit avoir récemment réalisé, avec quelques amis, de nouveaux investissements dans SLAB, mais rejette l’idée selon laquelle la plateforme serait un simple projet de centre de données flottant pour l’intelligence artificielle. Plusieurs start-ups se sont déjà positionnées pour exploiter la mer et l’énergie générée par les vagues ou les marées au profit de centres de données, comme Panthalassa, basée à Portland, dans l’Oregon, qui a levé 140 millions de dollars en mai et bénéficie notamment du soutien de Peter Thiel. En Écosse, Mocean Energy a annoncé en juillet son projet d’installer des serveurs d’IA sur des flotteurs en mer, alimentés par les vagues, des panneaux solaires et des batteries, refroidis par l’eau de mer environnante et reliés à la terre par satellite The Long-Running Climate Reporting Saga That Is Giving Companies Whiplash », The Wall Street Journal , 16 novembre 2026.'> 7 . Afin d’échapper aux réglementations des États fédérés tout en restant dans les eaux américaines, SLAB – si le projet venait à voir le jour – devrait se trouver à au moins trois milles nautiques des côtes, soit environ 5,5 kilomètres, la limite des eaux relevant des États. Les activités de la plateforme resteraient théoriquement soumises aux normes et lois fédérales. Trump a proposé, durant la campagne pour la présidentielle de 2024, la création de « Freedom Cities », des villes nouvelles bâties sur des terres fédérales et soustraites à une partie des réglementations fédérales. Plusieurs groupes représentant des projets de villes autonomes affirment avoir rencontré des membres de l’administration Trump et échangé avec des élus dans les semaines qui ont suivi son retour au pouvoir, en janvier 2025 ‘Startup City’ Groups Say They’re Meeting Trump Officials to Push for Deregulated ‘Freedom Cities’ », Wired , 7 mars 2025.'> 8 . La Freedom Cities Coalition, créée par une société liée à Próspera, travaille notamment à la rédaction d’un projet de loi qui permettrait au Congrès d’approuver par avance la création de ces villes par des accords entre États. L’article Pour échapper aux régulations, Palmer Luckey veut délocaliser des activités stratégiques sur une plateforme en mer est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Untenable stalemate
items.description: NEARLY nine months into a conflict of choice that has rattled economies from Europe to Asia, there seem to be few agreeable options for the US where ending the Iran war is concerned. No one — perhaps apart from Israel and some hawks in Washington — wants an escalation, while coming to an agreement on Iran’s terms would result in considerable embarrassment for Donald Trump. However, Pakistan, which has played a crucial mediatory role in the conflict, and other regional states still have expectations that a negotiated settlement can be reached. As Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar told the ECO meeting on Monday, “we have not given up hope” for peace. The Iranian foreign minister was also in Islamabad for the event, and praised Pakistan’s efforts to broker peace. But the most sincere efforts by Pakistan or any other mediator will not bear fruit unless there is clarity in Washington. President Trump, as has been his practice, has oscillated between saying the war is “effectively over”, and threatening fresh strikes if talks fall through. This cognitive dissonance must end. Over the past few days, there have been some low-key military engagements between the US and Iran. The US had reportedly attacked facilities on the Iranian coast, while Tehran hit back by targeting American sites in Bahrain. These exchanges have the potential to get out of hand and spark a bigger confrontation. Which is why the quicker the matter is resolved, the better. The collective voice from the states of this region is clearly against war, while the majority of the American people also appear uninterested in fresh clashes with Iran. Therefore, it is time the White House faced the bitter reality that its ill-conceived Iran campaign — fuelled by bad Israeli advice — has failed, and committed to resolving the imbroglio peacefully. The option of attacking Iran again must be taken off the table by the US. In fact, there should be a positive response to the Iranian proposal currently on the table, specifically where lifting the blockade, ending sanctions, and allowing access to Tehran’s funds goes. This may seem like ‘capitulation’ to Mr Trump, but these matters should have been thought through before launching this disastrous war. Tehran should also show flexibility, particularly where free and unhindered access through the Strait of Hormuz is concerned. Should Washington opt for the diplomatic off-ramp, it will find that regional states, particularly Pakistan, Qatar and others, will be happy to facilitate dialogue. However, indecision and a damaging status quo that is affecting regional peace and the global economy cannot be allowed to continue. It is time the Trump administration did the right thing. Published in Dawn, November 18th, 2026

items.title: 15,000-tonne LPG cargo arrives from Abu Dhabi under new policy to ease shortages
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The government on Wednesday said it received the first cargo of 15,000 tonnes of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from Abu Dhabi after it introduced policy changes earlier this month to arrange imports through state-owned enterprises (SOEs) to ease supply constraints and contain rising prices in winter. In a statement, the Petroleum Division said that SSGC LPG Limited (SSL) – a subsidiary of the state-run Sui Southern Gas Company Limited (SSGCL) – had imported a record 15,000 metric tonnes of LPG cargo, the largest of its kind that berthed at Engro Vopak Terminal Limited (EVTL). The shipment marks the first “major” import under the new LPG guidelines aimed at ensuring the availability of LPG at affordable rates for the public, the statement said. The SSL arranged the cargo through competitive bidding at a price yet to be disclosed by the company. Petroleum Division officials said the company would publish details of the pricing components on its website in a couple of days, but claimed the SSL import had already dented market prices by Rs100 to Rs120 per kg. Separately, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervez Malik informally told journalists that another shipment arranged by Pakistan State Oil (PSO) was on its way to Karachi and would reach over the next two days, followed by others. He said LPG availability would address the pricing distortions in the market. On November 3, the federal cabinet approved new LPG pricing guidelines to enable SOEs to play a leading role in securing LPG supplies. Previously, formal sector companies had exited imports due to regulatory constraints that prevented them from recovering procurement costs. Under the cabinet decision, the government also directed state-owned companies to lead LPG imports and strengthen the country’s supply chain, especially in winter. The increased influx of LPG is expected to further improve market availability, ease supply constraints and help bring prices down through greater product availability. It will also enhance supplies to hilly, remote and far-flung areas, particularly during peak winter season. A welcome ceremony was held at Port Qasim to mark the arrival of the shipment, with Special Secretary Petroleum Mirza Nasir ud Din Mashood as the chief guest. SLL Managing Director Jawad Ali Khan, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) Senior Executive Director (LPG) Sarmad Aslam, and other senior officials were present at the occasion, according to the statement. Speaking at the ceremony, Petroleum Special Secretary Mirza Nasiruddin Mashood said that the prime minister and the petroleum minister had issued directives to take effective measures to ensure LPG availability to the public. He said the arrival of the record shipment marked a new era for the LPG sector and would further strengthen the country’s supply chain. He congratulated SLL on this achievement. The government said the LPG pricing change was meant to create competition in the market through procurement of LPG by four SOEs on government-to-government (G2G) and business-to-business (B2B) arrangements and flood the market. LPG, often described as the poor man’s fuel, has been in short supply even before the onset of winter as western borders faced disruption. Resultantly, unscrupulous elements started taking advantage by selling the product to consumers at Rs700 to Rs800 per kilogramme against Rs295 per kg maximum price set by Ogra for November . LPG pricing The government is working with the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) to provide LPG to the “most deserving and vulnerable” at Rs300-350 per kg through a subsidy mechanism to be funded by a new account arising from the differential between LPG import parity price and auction of local LPG produced by refineries and exploration and production companies under a clawback mechanism. The SOEs — PSO, Pakistan LNG Ltd, SSL and Parco-LPG — have been engaged with various suppliers from Saudi Arabia and Oman for LPG supply. Apart from imports through SOEs, the cabinet has also decided to put an end to the existing quota system for domestic LPG enjoyed by influential groups, and local producers would auction their LPG in 5 to 10 tonnes through a competitive process under Ogra and the Petroleum Division’s supervision. Under the new arrangement, these SOEs would announce the base price —freight-on-board (FOB) linked with the Saudi Aramco contract price (CP) — along with other costs including the premium, freight (CFR), insurance, incidental costs and import taxes actually incurred by PSO or any other SOE in the preceding month (monthly average landed cost) on their websites. Ogra would stop issuance of price notification for local (or imported) LPG forthwith. The local producers shall be entitled to this producer price only discovered through auction and the differential between the producer price (Saudi CP-linked FOB) and the base price of PSO shall be deposited in the fund account to subsidise poor consumers through BISP. The private sector has been demanding an end to the Saudi-CP-linked price, considering that most of the imports originate from other countries, including Iran and Oman. In case of no imports by SOEs in a month, the preceding month’s premium, incidentals and taxes shall apply with the current month’s CP on the pattern of diesel and petrol pricing. There would be an increase in margins for LPG marketing and importing companies to Rs50,000 per tonne floor instead of the existing Rs35,000 per tonne as inflation adjustment since the 2016 LPG policy. Ten per cent of the indigenous LPG produced by exploration and production (E&P) companies, refineries and other producers shall be allocated to state-owned marketers at producer price, to guarantee supply to the northern areas, Gilgit-Baltistan and other remote, hilly and hard-to-reach areas for supply through cylinders or already installed LPG air-mix plants. The remaining 90pc will be allocated, through a transparent monthly auction with a floor price equal to 5pc of import-parity price of PSO, to prequalified bottlers to increase investment in infrastructure and storage, cylinders in circulation, geographical reach and operational capability, with safeguards against cartelisation. Ogra would be required to convene product review meetings on the pattern of oil products to ascertain supply-chain position, including the import plan and winter stock planning, and instruct specific import volumes to SOEs to ensure demand and supply balance in the market, especially during the winter.

items.title: Communiqué : Avis de recrutement d’un Chef de service Finances et Comptabilité (H/F)
items.description: COMPETENCE FOR ALL INSTITUTE (CFA-I), cabinet spécialisé dans le développement du capital humain et la transformation des organisations, recrute pour le compte de l'un de ses clients, un établissement d'enseignement supérieur privé de référence basé à Ouagadougou, un(e) Chef (fe) de Service Finances et Comptabilité. Votre mission : assurer le pilotage, la coordination et la supervision des activités financières, budgétaires et comptables, tout en contribuant à la fiabilité de l'information financière et au respect des procédures internes et de la réglementation en vigueur. VOS PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS Piloter le budget et la performance financière: coordonner l'élaboration du budget annuel, suivre son exécution, analyser les écarts et proposer les mesures correctives. Superviser la comptabilité: veiller à la bonne tenue de la comptabilité générale et, le cas échéant, analytique, à la justification des comptes, aux clôtures et à la préparation des états financiers. Sécuriser les dépenses: contrôler la conformité financière et documentaire des dossiers, la disponibilité budgétaire ainsi que le respect des procédures d'engagement et de paiement. Assurer le suivi de la trésorerie: superviser les recettes et dépenses, les rapprochements bancaires, les opérations de caisse et les prévisions de trésorerie. Coordonner le suivi financier de la paie travailler avec les ressources humaines sur les salaires, cotisations sociales, prélèvements fiscaux et autres éléments de rémunération. Contrôler les opérations d'achat: vérifier les factures et pièces justificatives et assurer le suivi financier des commandes avec les services concernés. Encadrer l'équipe: organiser et superviser le travail de l'équipe comptable et de caisse, répartir les tâches et veiller à l'application du contrôle interne. Produire le reporting: élaborer les tableaux de bord, rapports périodiques et analyses utiles à la prise de décision de la Direction Générale. Assurer les relations avec les partenaires externes: mettre à disposition les informations nécessaires aux audits, contrôles et travaux du Commissaire aux comptes. LE PROFIL QUE NOUS RECHERCHONS Formation être titulaire d'un diplôme de niveau BAC+3 minimum en Finance, Comptabilité, Gestion financière, Audit ou dans un domaine équivalent pertinent. Expérience: justifier d'au moins cinq (05) années d'expérience professionnelle pertinente en finance, comptabilité, contrôle financier ou gestion budgétaire, avec une expérience significative en supervision d'équipe ou en coordination d'activités financières et comptables. VOS COMPÉTENCES TECHNIQUES Bonne maîtrise des principes et normes comptables applicables, notamment du référentiel SYSCOHADA; Maîtrise de la gestion budgétaire, de l'analyse financière et du suivi de la trésorerie; Maîtrise des procédures de contrôle des dépenses, des engagements et des paiements; Bonne connaissance des obligations fiscales et sociales liées aux opérations financières et à la paie; Capacité à élaborer, analyser et présenter des états financiers, des tableaux de bord et des rapports de gestion; Bonne maîtrise des outils informatiques de gestion comptable et financière ainsi que des tableurs; Connaissance des dispositifs de contrôle interne, de gestion des risques financiers et de sécurisation des opérations; Maîtrise du système des SA. LES QUALITÉS QUI FERONT LA DIFFÉRENCE Rigueur et intégrité Sens élevé de la confidentialité Esprit d'analyse et de synthèse Leadership et aptitude à encadrer une équipe Organisation et gestion des priorités Autonomie et réactivité Force de proposition Excellentes capacités de communication et de collaboration Sens des responsabilités et orientation résultats. CONDITIONS DE CANDIDATURE Les candidat(e)s intéressé(e)s et répondant aux critères sont invité(e)s à constituer un dossier comprenant: Un curriculum vitae actualisé et détaillé; Une lettre de motivation adressée au Directeur Général de CFA-I; Les copies des diplômes et attestations pertinentes. Transmission des candidatures: les dossiers sont à envoyer à travers le lien : https://competenceforall.com/jobs/chef-de-service-finances-et-comptabilite-h-f-44 avec pour objet : « Candidature au poste de Chef(fe) de Service Finances et Comptabilité » . DATE LIMITE DE CANDIDATURE: 23 NOVEMBRE 2026 À 17 H Seul(e)s les candidat(e)s présélectionné(e)s seront contacté(e)s pour la suite du processus. Le Directeur Général Boureima GUIRO

items.title: Nationale Kankan-Siguiri : Un accident fait 4 morts à Norako
items.description: Un accident de la circulation s'est produit ce mercredi 18 novembre 2026 ,sur l'axe routier Kankan-Siguiri, plus précisément dans le secteur de Norako, situé à Balimana Dalaba dans la sous-préfecture de Fodécariah Balimana. Le bilan provisoire fait état de quatre personnes décédées. Selon les informations recueillies sur place, le drame implique un poids lourd et un véhicule personnel. D'après les témoignages concordants, les deux camions se seraient frottés avant de se renverser sur la chaussée. C'est dans ces circonstances qu'un véhicule en provenance de Siguiri, est entré en collision avec l'un des camions immobilisés. Le choc a été d'une violence extrême. Les quatre occupants du véhicule léger n'ont pas survécu. « Nous avions été informés qu'un accident s'est produit sur la route Kankan-Siguiri juste à Norako. Mais sur place, nous avons constaté quatre (4) morts. Il y a deux gros camions qui se sont frottés ici, un est tombé à côté, l'autre aussi. Le petit véhicule venait de Siguiri, il est venu taper sur le camion qui était par là et les personnes qui étaient dans ce véhicule sont toutes mortes », a expliqué Lanciné Doumbouya de la coix rouge de Balimana. Selon Lanciné Doumbouya, les agents de la gendarmerie se sont rapidement rendus sur les lieux pour procéder aux premières constatations d'usage et sécuriser la zone. Les corps sans vie des victimes ont été transportés à la morgue de l'hôpital de Siguiri . Ce nouvel accident mortel vient relancer le débat sur la sécurité routière sur l'axe Kankan-Siguiri, une voie stratégique pour l'économie guinéenne mais tristement célèbre pour la fréquence des drames liés aux poids lourds.

items.title: £190m corruption case: IHC directs proper medical care, hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi as per prison rules
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Wednesday directed prison authorities to ensure medical care and hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi as per prison rules, while adjourning the hearing of appeals filed by her and her husband, PTI founder Imran Khan, against their convictions in the £190 million case for seven days. The couple is serving prison sentences in the £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case. On January 17, 2025, an accountability court in Islamabad sentenced Imran to 14 years in prison and Bushra to seven years in the case. Both subsequently challenged their convictions before the IHC. On Monday, Bushra had filed a fresh criminal miscellaneous application seeking the production of her complete medical record before the court and directions for her immediate transfer to a specialised hospital. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif granted Barrister Salman Safdar, counsel for the PTI founder, seven days to prepare arguments on the appeals. During the proceedings, the court also took up a fresh miscellaneous application filed on behalf of Bushra, raising concerns about her deteriorating eyesight, need for surgery, possible post-operative complications and the medical facilities available to her in prison. After hearing arguments from her counsel, Sardar Latif Khosa, the bench directed the prison authorities to ensure cleanliness in her cell, arrange an examination by a specialist doctor from a hospital and provide all necessary medical facilities in accordance with jail rules. The court further directed Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik to ensure that its order was implemented through the relevant prison authorities. Khosa informed the court that Bushra had told her legal team that she required surgery and that there were concerns about the possible deterioration of her eyesight. He stressed that Bushra’s health required immediate attention, particularly in view of the risk of infection following surgery. Reading out the contents of the miscellaneous application, Khosa also referred to incidents allegedly occurring inside the prison. He told the court that seven small snakes had reportedly been found in Bushra’s cell and killed by a prison official identified as Sibtain. The area was subsequently sealed with cement, according to the application. Khosa argued that prison conditions could expose his client to infections, making special precautions necessary, particularly if she underwent surgery. Justice Dogar said the court had taken note of the concerns and would ensure that Bushra received all facilities permissible under prison rules. He directed that the difficulties highlighted in the application should not be allowed to recur and assured Khosa that the former first lady was in safe hands. Justice Dogar also recalled that health-related matters had previously been referred to the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), but said the present application would be dealt with in accordance with the bench’s jurisdiction. Khosa, however, maintained that the risk of infection following surgery remained a serious concern. He added that even if bail were granted, Bushra could remain in the court’s custody. When the counsel referred to the fresh application concerning Bushra’s health, Justice Dogar reminded him that he had earlier undertaken to commence arguments on the main appeals after meeting the PTI founder. Khosa confirmed that he and Barrister Safdar had met Imran in accordance with the court’s previous direction and had submitted their respective affidavits . Justice Dogar subsequently directed that arguments on the appeals commence. Khosa also informed the bench that Safdar would argue Imran’s appeal, while he would represent Bushra. Safdar requested permission to address the court and sought live broadcasting of the proceedings in the appeals, arguing that the case had attracted considerable public attention. He said that although the bench had described the matter as a routine case at the previous hearing, proceedings in the case involving former military ruler General Pervez Musharraf had been broadcast live. Referring to the live broadcasts of proceedings in various cases before the Supreme Court and high courts, Safdar urged the bench to allow the appeals to be broadcast live as well. He said he would submit a formal application in this regard. The PTI founder’s sisters, Noreen Khan and Dr Uzma, were present in the courtroom, along with PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and other party leaders. National Accountability Bureau Prosecutor General Sohail Nasir, prosecutors Javed Arshad and Rafay Maqsood, and Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik also attended the proceedings. Tight security arrangements were in place inside and around the IHC. Barrister Safdar met Imran and Bushra at Adiala jail on Nov 2, 2026. This was his first meeting with Imran after seven months and with Bushra in 11 months, lasting 40 minutes. On Nov 11, 2026, Barrister Safdar and Khosa also met Imran and Bushra at Adiala jail for nearly three hours, following IHC orders. On Monday, both lawyers submitted affidavits to the IHC, detailing their Nov 11 meeting with the incarcerated couple at Adiala jail. The lawyers stated in their affidavits that Bushra complained of severely impaired vision in both eyes following her previous surgical procedure . She also told them that she could see only to a limited extent while wearing spectacles and was virtually unable to see without them. Imran’s lawyer issues legal notice to Adiala superintendent Meanwhile, Imran’s lawyer Khalid Yusuf Chaudhry issued a legal notice to Adiala jail’s superintendent, demanding that the PTI founder be transferred to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital (SIH) in compliance with the SC’s August 18 orders . The notice, posted on Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan’s X account, said Imran was transferred to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences despite the court’s order specifying he be shifted to Shifa International Hospital. Chaudhry said that Imran’s fundamental human, constitutional and legal rights must be protected. “He should be allowed to meet his family members and wife, have audio and video contact with his sons, and be provided with newspapers, books and television, as well as an hour of daily outdoor walking and exercise,” the legal notice said. It further added that keeping a prisoner in isolation and restricting his human contact under the pretext of security concerns was “unacceptable”. “Such conduct violates the Constitution of Pakistan and domestic and international laws concerning prisoners’ rights,” the notice said. It demanded that the Adiala jail superintendent transfer Imran to Shifa International Hospital without delay, fully comply with the court’s orders and restore all his legal and human rights. Additional input from Ikram Junaidi
